newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil industry head hopes for stable currency.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil industry head hopes for stable currency.

text.p: Japan's oil industry chief said on Wednesday that he hoped to see foreign exchange rates stabilise and not fluctuate rapidly.
Petroleum Association of Japan (PAJ) Chairman Yuji Idemitsu told a news conference that having a stable currency was important for the industry.
"It can be 110 yen (to the dollar) or 120 yen (to the dollar), but we'd like to see it stabilise and not fluctuate so much," Idemitsu, who is also president of Idemitsu Kosan KK, said.
Japan relies heavily on imported crude oil for its energy needs, and foreign exchange rates have a huge bearing on oil companies' earnings.
Japanese oil companies take into account crude oil prices and foreign exchange rates to review their wholesale oil product prices every month.
The Japanese currency traded around 124 yen to the dollar on Wednesday.
